thread:
emma: Heads up — noticed a pretty bad perf regression in canary after yesterday's runtime merge. Token/sec dropped ~30%, p95 latency up, queues building.

emma: Quick numbers from canary vs baseline: before=3500 tok/s, after=2400 tok/s (same model, same batch config).

emma: Logs show a lot more time in scheduler wait:
```
scheduler: queued_time_ms=45 -> 180
batch_size_histogram: {1: 4200, 2: 800, 4: 120} (was {1: 1200, 2: 2200, 4: 700})
kv-cache: miss_rate 0.08 -> 0.27
```

raj: Yikes. Which PR was merged? Any suspects?

emma: PR #482 (adaptive-batching + kernel-picker tweak) and PR #489 (kv-cache eviction tuning) landed in the same window.

olivia: I'm worried about the kernel-picker change that added a small-batch penalty — intended to avoid bad kernels on <8 token seqs. Could push the scheduler to split more and wait.

olivia: Also saw a recent change to KV cache eviction threshold from 0.6->0.8 in #489, that could cause more evictions (higher miss rate) if memory pressure differs in canary.

dan: CI perf job showed green though — but it uses synthetic traces with different seq distribution. This smells like a workload distribution mismatch.

ci-bot: perf-ci: Benchmark suite ran on commit 9a7b3c4 — all microbenchmarks within noise except 'continuous-batching/tokens-per-sec' which dropped by 28% (p<0.01).

marco: Let's bisect quickly. Steps:
1) git bisect start HEAD base
2) mark good at base (before merges)
3) mark bad at HEAD (after merges)
4) run perf-ci relevant test locally (quick flags)

emma: Running the bisect now, running the tokens/sec microbenchmark against the runtime image per-commit. Will post suspect commit.

emma: Bisect found culprit: commit 9a7b3c4 -> "scheduler: introduce small-batch kernel penalty" (from #482).

raj: Nice find. That explains the batch size histogram shift — scheduler is preferring smaller batches to avoid kernel mismatch but adding wait, net effect worse throughput.

olivia: Can we patch the penalty to be softer (or conditional on observed seq-length distribution)? Maybe only apply penalty when seq_len>threshold and kernel actually harmful.

emma: Quick experiment: I built a patch that disables the penalty and redeployed to canary. Numbers: reverted penalty -> tok/s back to ~3450, batch histogram back to expected, kv-cache miss remained high though (0.24).

ra: (typo) raj: That suggests kernel penalty was main driver. KV miss increase still there but less impactful.

olivia: For KV cache, we should also look at the eviction change in #489 — if memory tuning differs across clusters it could amplify misses. We should not ship both changes together.

marco: Agree. Options: revert scheduler penalty commit for now, and open a follow-up to make kernel-picker adapt at runtime (use rolling metrics).

emma: I'm marking the canary as degraded on the rollout and requesting immediate revert.

deploy-bot: Revert PR created -> r/revert-9a7b3c4. Triggering canary rollback to previous image.

sre-bot: Canary rollback started at 1762805620. Monitoring metrics...

sre-bot: Canary metrics: tok/s climbing back to baseline within 3m. p95 latency back to normal. queue_length dropping.

emma: Confirmed — revert fixed throughput. Raising a rollout-blocker for the combined change set.

raj: I'll follow up with a smaller kernel-picker change proposal: add runtime probe to pick kernel and avoid penalty unless it demonstrably improves latency in production. Also adding canary perf test to block merges that change scheduler heuristics.

olivia: I'll open PRs: one revert + one safer adaptive approach. Also will revert kv-cache eviction tweak for now.

dan: Good. Also add a test that runs the continuous-batching microbench with realistic seq distribution so CI catches this next time.

emma: Thanks everyone. Moving this to postmortem/rollback notes if needed. :thumbsup:

olivia: small follow-ups: paste the bisect command I used for reference:
```
git bisect start 9a7b3c4 HEAD
git bisect good <old-good-commit>
git bisect bad HEAD
# run ./tools/perf/bench_continuous_batch --model gpt-small
```

marco: Nice, saving that. Closing loop once PRs merged and CI updated.

emma: cc @product (FYI rollback triggered)

raj: Thanks — learned to be careful bundling scheduler and cache changes together.

emma: End of thread.
